subject: [PATCH RFC fstests] generic: add a test for multigrain timestamps

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Suggested exposing the support for multi-grain timestamps from the kernel by adding a flag to stx_attributes. This would simplify the test and make it more robust.
reviews.raw_body:
On Tue, Oct 27, 2026 at 09:58:50AM -0400, Jeff Layton wrote:
> Ensure that the mtime and ctime apparently change, even when there are
> multiple writes in quick succession. Since this is opt-in for in-kernel
> filesystems and there is no way to test for this feature in userland,
> limit it to just ext4, f2fs, btrfs, tmpfs and xfs for now.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
> ---
> I'd like to start testing this to make sure it doesn't break, but it's
> not universally supported on all filesystems. Is an explicit allowlist
> like this the right approach?

Can we please expose the fact that multi-grain timestamp are supported
from the kernel?  This seems like it would be just one bit we'd need
in sttx or something similar.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton
reviews.summary: Agreed to consider Christoph's suggestion and explore adding a flag to stx_attributes. This would allow the test to be more straightforward and reliable.
reviews.raw_body:
On Wed, 2026-10-28 at 08:54 -0700, Christoph Hellwig wrote:
> On Tue, Oct 27, 2026 at 09:58:50AM -0400, Jeff Layton wrote:
> > Ensure that the mtime and ctime apparently change, even when there are
> > multiple writes in quick succession. Since this is opt-in for in-kernel
> > filesystems and there is no way to test for this feature in userland,
> > limit it to just ext4, f2fs, btrfs, tmpfs and xfs for now.
> > 
> > Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
> > ---
> > I'd like to start testing this to make sure it doesn't break, but it's
> > not universally supported on all filesystems. Is an explicit allowlist
> > like this the right approach?
> 
> Can we please expose the fact that multi-grain timestamp are supported
> from the kernel?  This seems like it would be just one bit we'd need
> in sttx or something similar.

I'd been resisting that, but maybe it's a good idea. I'll see what I
can come up with. We can probably just add a flag to stx_attributes?
-- 
Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

2026-10-28.patch_summary: This patch adds a test for multigrain timestamps, which are fine-grained timestamps that can change even when multiple writes occur in quick succession. The test is limited to five filesystems (ext4, f2fs, btrfs, tmpfs, and xfs) because it's not universally supported on all filesystems yet. The patch includes a new Makefile target and a C program that tests the multigrain timestamp functionality.
